prize_parts.citation: For developing methods to estimate demand, competition and industry dynamics from market data, which made structural empirical industrial organisation a quantitative basis for analysing market power, mergers and regulation.

statement.case_for: B001 gives the clearest combination of conceptual advance, breadth of use and durability on the shortlist. Random-coefficients demand with endogenous prices, the Olley-Pakes production-function approach and the Ericson-Pakes framework for dynamic industries turned industrial organisation into a field where demand, markups, entry and welfare can be measured in a disciplined way. The tools are now routine in merger review, antitrust and regulation. They have also spread to trade, health, environmental and macro-adjacent work on productivity and market power, which is why I judge this a contribution to economics generally and not only to a subfield. The core papers are about 30 years old and have been tested in practice, so timing is not a concern. Pakes anchors the three methodological strands. Berry's inversion and his BLP work are essential to making demand estimation feasible. Bresnahan's New Empirical IO programme and his early demand-based estimation of market power in differentiated-product markets supplied the question to which the later tools were the answer. I judge that a citation grounded in that lineage is better attributed than a narrower reading of BLP alone.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation is attribution. The ballot entry lists seven names and the field has several interlocking strands: demand estimation, production-function estimation, dynamic games and the conceptual programme. Any three-person cut leaves out real contributors, and the choice between Levinsohn and Bresnahan for the third slot is a close judgement. A second concern is whether the Committee should reward a toolkit rather than a substantive finding. Structural IO also has known weaknesses: sensitivity to functional-form assumptions, numerical fragility in BLP implementations and weak-identification problems. These are documented, but they limit how much weight applied results can carry.

responses.point: Dreber ranks B001 first with Pakes, Berry and Levinsohn. She ties the 1995 demand paper most closely to the BLP trio and notes that Pakes also led the dynamic-games work. She treats the numerical and identification problems as well documented and largely addressed.
responses.response: I agree that the 1995 paper belongs to Berry, Levinsohn and Pakes, and that the numerical and identification problems are known and have largely been addressed. That is why I do not count them as disqualifying. Where I differ is on the third name. A citation tied narrowly to the BLP paper would favour Levinsohn. The accomplishment I would reward is wider: estimating demand and supply together to measure market power, production-function methods, and dynamic industry models. Bresnahan's early estimation of market power with differentiated-product demand systems is part of that lineage, and Levinsohn's role is mostly captured in a single paper. I accept that this is a close call, and I would not treat a Levinsohn version as a scientific error.

responses.point: Teorell treats Bresnahan, Reiss, Benkard and Levin as secondary or adjacent to the BLP core and leaves them out of the trio. He also asks whether the economics-wide significance outweighs the specialised character of the field.
responses.response: I agree about Reiss, Benkard and Levin. Their contributions are real but are extensions or applications of the core, so the three-person limit is not a hard constraint for them. I do not agree that Bresnahan is adjacent. His work on measuring market power is among the foundations of the empirical programme the later toolkit made operational. On breadth, the evidence in favour is use well outside IO. Demand estimation and production-function methods are applied in trade, health and productivity analysis, and the dynamic-oligopoly framework is a template for modelling heterogeneous firms. I think that answers the specialised-field concern better than the argument from narrowness.

responses.point: Fredriksson ranks B002 first and B001 second. He proposes Pakes, Berry and Bresnahan, and acknowledges that dropping Levinsohn leaves the BLP credit imperfect. For B002 he regards Kiyotaki and Moore as the clear origin of collateral amplification, with Gertler extending it, and notes that the 2022 prize overlaps in subject.
responses.response: We agree on the B001 trio, and his remark that excluding Levinsohn is imperfect is fair. It is the main cost of my version. On B002 I agree that the Kiyotaki-Moore mechanism is a deep and general contribution, and I keep it as my first alternative. I still prefer B001 as the first-order choice because B002's remaining attribution question, whether to add Gertler given the Bernanke-Gertler-Gilchrist strand and the 2022 prize, is harder to resolve cleanly. The overlap with a recent prize on banks and crises also raises a novelty question that B001 does not face. I would not claim B002 is the weaker science, only that its prize claim is more entangled.

responses.point: Hassler ranks B001 first and B049 second, with a Taylor, Woodford and Calvo trio. He treats B002 as a clean Kiyotaki-Moore pair, and notes that adding Gertler would dilute it.
responses.response: I share the view that Kiyotaki and Moore are the clean pair for B002. On B049 I agree that the policy influence is very large, but that influence is not what separates candidates for me. The attribution problem is. Calvo, Taylor and Woodford are one defensible trio, yet Gali, Christiano, Eichenbaum, Gertler and Smets all have strong claims, and the 2021-23 inflation episode has reopened questions about the framework. I ranked B049 fourth in my opening and would not move it above B001 or B002, where the credit is more separable.

uncertainties: Whether Bresnahan or Levinsohn should take the third slot with Pakes and Berry. I have no independent evidence that settles it.
Whether the Committee wants a methods-and-tools prize for structural estimation or a narrower citation tied to a single paper.
How much weight to put on known numerical and identification fragilities in BLP-type estimation. I have not independently verified citation counts or adoption evidence.
Whether B002 would be easier to settle if the Committee agrees on a Kiyotaki-Moore pair without Gertler, given the 2022 prize.
Whether Helpman's two ballot entries (B050, B021) change how credit is allocated in the trade area.
statement.conflict_note: None apparent from the supplied profile for B001. I have no listed co-authorship or institutional tie to Pakes, Berry, Bresnahan or Levinsohn, and none to Kiyotaki or Moore. My listed co-authors, including the chair John Hassler, co-opted member Timo Boppart and others, do not appear among the credited names on the alternatives I name (B002, B050). My work on heterogeneous-agent macro and growth is adjacent to some shortlisted topics, such as technology and inequality in B013 and misallocation in B039, but I do not propose those.
